options.label: A type of sound wave
options.feedback: Sound waves are mechanical vibrations that need a medium to travel; visible light is electromagnetic radiation that can travel through a vacuum.

options.label: A form of heat energy
options.feedback: Heat can be transferred by radiation, but visible light is specifically electromagnetic radiation that the human eye can perceive; heat is not the same thing.

options.label: Electromagnetic radiation that the human eye can perceive
options.feedback: That is exactly what visible light is—a part of the electromagnetic spectrum, with wavelengths roughly from 400 to 700 nanometers, that our eyes can detect.

options.label: A stream of tiny solid particles
options.feedback: Light behaves as both particles and waves, but these particles are massless photons, not solid matter.

items.ok_line: Visible light is the electromagnetic radiation our eyes can see.
items.ko_line: Think about what our eyes can detect.
items.exp_text: Visible light is electromagnetic radiation that can be perceived by the human eye. It lies in the range of wavelengths from about 400 to 700 nanometers, sitting between infrared and ultraviolet on the electromagnetic spectrum.

items.prompt: Which of these is NOT part of the visible spectrum?

options.label: Radio waves
options.feedback: Radio waves have much longer wavelengths and lower frequencies than visible light; they are a different part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

options.label: Red light
options.feedback: Red light is at the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum, so it is part of what we see.

options.label: Violet light
options.feedback: Violet is at the short-wavelength end of the visible range, so it is definitely visible.

options.label: Green light
options.feedback: Green light sits in the middle of the visible spectrum, so it is part of what the human eye can perceive.

items.ok_line: Radio waves are invisible to the human eye.
items.ko_line: The visible spectrum includes colours from red to violet.
items.exp_text: The visible spectrum is the range of wavelengths the human eye can see. Radio waves have far longer wavelengths, so they are not visible light; they belong to another part of the electromagnetic spectrum.

items.prompt: What is the main source of natural light on Earth?

options.label: The Moon
options.feedback: The Moon only reflects sunlight; it does not produce its own visible light.

options.label: Fire
options.feedback: Fire is a source of light for humans, but it is not the main natural source on Earth.

options.label: Electric lamps
options.feedback: Electric lamps are artificial sources, not natural ones.

options.label: The Sun
options.feedback: The Sun is indeed the main natural source of light for our planet.

items.ok_line: The Sun is the main natural light source.
items.ko_line: What shines all day and lights the whole Earth?
items.exp_text: The Sun is the main source of natural light on Earth. It emits visible light that reaches us, and without it our world would be dark.

options.label: A wave of the electromagnetic field
options.feedback: Waves are part of light's behaviour, but a photon is the particle-like quantum of light, not the wave itself.

options.label: A single quantum of light
options.feedback: A photon is a single, massless elementary particle, a quantum of light.

options.label: A charged particle found in atoms
options.feedback: That describes electrons or protons; photons have no charge and are not parts of atoms.

options.label: A tiny mirror that reflects light
options.feedback: Mirrors are objects that reflect light; they are not what light is made of.

items.ok_line: A photon is one quantum of light.
items.ko_line: Light has both wave and particle aspects.
items.exp_text: A photon is a single, massless elementary particle of light. Light behaves as a wave in many situations, but when it interacts with matter as a particle, the particles are photons.

items.prompt: Which of these is listed as a primary property of light?

options.label: Temperature
options.feedback: Temperature is a property of matter, not of light itself.

options.label: Colour
options.feedback: Colour results from the wavelength of light, but it is not listed as a primary property—wavelength or frequency is.

options.label: Intensity
options.feedback: Intensity is indeed one of the primary properties of light.

options.label: Hardness
options.feedback: Hardness describes materials; light is not a material.

items.ok_line: Intensity is a primary property of light.
items.ko_line: Look for the fundamental characteristics of light.
items.exp_text: The primary properties of light are intensity, propagation direction, frequency or wavelength spectrum, and polarization.

items.prompt: What happens to the speed of light when it travels in water compared to in a vacuum?

options.label: It is slower in water
options.feedback: In water the speed is about 3/4 of its speed in a vacuum, so yes, it is slower.

options.label: It is faster in water
options.feedback: Light moves fastest in a vacuum; no ordinary material can make it go faster.

options.label: It stays the same in both
options.feedback: Light's speed changes when it enters a transparent substance like water.

options.label: It stops completely in water
options.feedback: Light does not stop; it slows down but continues travelling.

items.ok_line: Light travels slower in water than in vacuum.
items.exp_text: In a vacuum, light travels at about 299,792,458 m/s, but in water its effective speed is only about three-quarters of that value.

items.prompt: What does the term 'light' mean in physics in its broadest sense?

options.label: Only visible light from the Sun
options.feedback: In physics, 'light' is not limited to sunlight or to what we can see.

options.label: Just the colours of the rainbow
options.feedback: The rainbow is visible light, but physics uses a broader meaning for the word.

options.label: Anything that illuminates a room
options.feedback: That is a practical meaning, not the broad physics definition.

options.label: Electromagnetic radiation of any wavelength
options.feedback: That is the broad physics meaning: gamma rays, X-rays, microwaves and radio waves are all considered light in this sense.

items.ok_line: In physics, light includes all electromagnetic radiation.
items.ko_line: Physics uses 'light' for more than just what you see.
items.exp_text: In physics, the term 'light' may refer to electromagnetic radiation of any wavelength, whether visible or not. So gamma rays, X-rays, microwaves and radio waves are also called light in this broad sense.

items.prompt: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum lies just beyond the red end of visible light?

options.label: Ultraviolet
options.feedback: Ultraviolet has shorter wavelengths and higher frequencies, so it lies beyond the violet end, not the red end.

options.label: X-rays
options.feedback: X-rays have even shorter wavelengths than ultraviolet, so they are far beyond the violet end.

options.label: Infrared
options.feedback: Infrared has longer wavelengths and lower frequencies than visible light, so it sits right after the red end.

options.label: Radio waves
options.feedback: Radio waves have very long wavelengths, but they are not the immediate neighbour; infrared lies between visible and radio in wavelength.

items.ok_line: Infrared lies just past the red end.
items.ko_line: Remember the order from red to violet.
items.exp_text: The visible band is bordered on its red side by infrared, which has longer wavelengths and lower frequencies. On the violet side is ultraviolet, with shorter wavelengths and higher frequencies.

items.prompt: What is the study of light and its interaction with matter called?

options.label: Mechanics
options.feedback: Mechanics is the study of motion and forces, not of light.

options.label: Optics
options.feedback: Optics is exactly the field that studies light and how it interacts with matter.

options.label: Acoustics
options.feedback: Acoustics is the study of sound, not light.

options.label: Thermodynamics
options.feedback: Thermodynamics deals with heat and energy transfer, not the study of light.

items.ok_line: Optics is the study of light.
items.ko_line: What subject would a light expert study?
items.exp_text: The study of light and the interaction of light and matter is termed optics, and it has different branches like geometrical, physical and quantum optics.

items.prompt: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?

options.label: 299,792,458 m/s
options.feedback: Yes, that is the exact defined speed of light in vacuum.

options.label: 300,000,000 m/s
options.feedback: That is a close approximation, but the exact defined value is 299,792,458 m/s.

options.label: 150,000,000 m/s
options.feedback: That is about half the actual speed of light in vacuum.

options.label: 1,000,000,000 m/s
options.feedback: That is much faster than the true speed of light in vacuum.

items.ok_line: Light travels at 299,792,458 m/s in vacuum.
items.exp_text: The speed of light in vacuum is defined to be exactly 299,792,458 metres per second, and all forms of electromagnetic radiation move at this same speed in vacuum.
